title: DNSmith provider manifest
description: One provider as DNSmith presents it. A manifest is the only thing the UI needs in order to render a provider's form, and for most providers it is also the only thing the updater needs in order to perform the update.

id.description: DNSmith's own identifier. Usually the same as engine.upstream_id, but it need not be: the upstream ID may change, this one must not.

categories.description: Drives the filters in the provider picker. A provider may sit in several.

popular.description: Shown in the picker's short list above the full catalogue.

adapter.description: Who performs the update. "native" means the declarative executor runs the request block below and no provider-specific code exists. "python" means a module under adapters/providers/ owns the flow, because the provider needs more than one step or a signature. "unported" is the transitional state: the provider is known, its form renders, but no updater backs it yet, so the UI offers it greyed out instead of pretending it works.

protocol.description: Which shape the native executor uses. "http" is a single request described entirely by the request block. "dyndns2" is the query-parameter protocol with its plain-text answer vocabulary; a named provider gives it a request block with a fixed endpoint, the generic one leaves it out because the user supplies the URL and the parameter names on the form. "custom_http" is the provider the user configures themselves and never has a request block.

module.description: Module name under adapters/providers/. Required for the python adapter.

multiple_records.description: Whether several host names can share one record entry, comma separated.

txt_records.description: Whether this provider's API can set and remove TXT records. Not used in v1; it is what a later ACME/DNS-01 feature would switch on, and recording it while the provider is being written costs nothing.

note.description: Shown next to the update interval so the limit is visible where it matters.

min_interval.description: Shortest interval DNSmith will allow for this provider, as a Go duration.

auth.description: Alternative ways to authenticate. Without this, every field in "fields" is offered at once — which is wrong for providers such as Cloudflare, where three mutually exclusive credential styles exist.

fields.description: Field IDs that make up this variant. All of them are required when it is chosen.

hint.description: Shown with the variant. This is where the minimum-permission advice belongs — at the field, not in a manual.

example.description: Placeholder values for the form, taken from the upstream documentation. Never real credentials.

notes.description: Provider quirks worth telling the user before they hit them.

generated.description: Provenance. Written by tools/manifest_merge.py, never by hand.

source.description: Where the content came from. Always providers/src/ since the rewrite.

request.description: The call that writes the record. Present for every native provider and absent for every python one.

lookup.description: Calls made before the update, each binding a value the update needs — a zone ID, a record ID. Steps run in order and may use what earlier steps bound. This is what lets a two-step API stay data rather than becoming a module.

create.description: The call that creates the record, used when a lookup with on_missing: create found nothing.

bindings.description: Extra values derived from the others, for providers that spell something standard their own way — a record type as 0 and 1 rather than A and AAAA. The alternative would be the executor learning a provider's name, which is the thing this design exists to avoid.

modes.description: Alternative ways to perform the update, chosen per record by the select field named in mode_field. The manifest's own top-level engine.protocol/request/lookup/create/bindings are the default mode — used whenever a record names no mode, an unrecognised one, or (for every record written before this existed) none at all. Each entry here replaces those wholesale for its id; nothing is merged between a mode and the default, or between two modes. Exists so a provider whose upstream API changed shape (a legacy endpoint next to a newer REST one, say) can offer both without either becoming its own catalogue entry or losing the record's IP history when the user switches.

protocol.description: Overrides engine.protocol for this mode. Omit to keep the manifest's own.

mode_field.description: ID of this provider's select field whose value chooses a mode. Its options must be exactly the keys of modes, one-to-one, and its default is the mode a record gets when the field is left at default. Required together with modes; meaningless without it.

url.description: Template. {name} is replaced by a field value, a runtime value, or a value a lookup step bound.

additionalProperties.description: Template. {name} is replaced by a field value, a runtime value, or a value a lookup step bound.

headers.description: Extra headers. The update's auth and headers are used unless overridden here.

additionalProperties.description: Template. {name} is replaced by a field value, a runtime value, or a value a lookup step bound.

omit_if_empty.description: JSON body keys to drop entirely, rather than send as "", when their templated value comes out empty. The default is to send "" — some providers read that as "clear this field" on purpose — so this exists for the opposite case: a provider that reads a family-specific key's mere presence as which record type is meant.

select.description: How to find the value in the answer.

path.description: Dotted path to the list (or object) in the answer. Omit for the answer itself.

where.description: Field/value pairs the entry must match. Comparison is textual, so a numeric ID and its string form both match.

additionalProperties.description: Template. {name} is replaced by a field value, a runtime value, or a value a lookup step bound.

take.description: Which field of the matched entry to bind.

into.description: Name this value is bound to, usable as {name} afterwards.

on_missing.description: What to do when nothing matches. "fail" reports that the record does not exist; "create" runs the create block instead of the update, which is how a record that is not there yet comes into being.

id.description: DNSmith's name for the field. This is what the stored record uses, so it must stay stable even if upstream renames its own.

maps_to.description: The key written into the engine's settings object. Defaults to id. This indirection is what stops an upstream rename from invalidating saved records.

when.description: Show this field only when another field has a given value. OVH needs it: its "mode" decides which credentials apply.

special_values.description: Values with a meaning of their own, such as Cloudflare's TTL 1 meaning "automatic".

extract.description: Where this field's value sits inside an update URL, for providers that hand their users a finished URL rather than the value. A pasted URL is reduced to the value before validation; anything that is not a URL is left alone.

url_query.description: Name of the query parameter holding the value.

url.description: Target URL, templated. Must be https unless allow_http is set.

allow_http.description: Permit a plain-http target. Only for providers that genuinely offer no TLS.

auth.description: An auth block, or a list of alternatives tried in order.

params.description: Query parameters. A value that resolves to empty is dropped, not sent blank.

additionalProperties.description: Template. {name} is replaced by a field value or by ipv4, ipv6, ip, hostname, domain, owner.
Template. {name} is replaced by a field value or by ipv4, ipv6, ip, hostname, domain, owner.

body.description: Request body before templating. Strings inside are templated at any depth.

omit_if_empty.description: JSON body keys to drop entirely, rather than send as "", when their templated value comes out empty. The default is to send "" — some providers read that as "clear this field" on purpose — so this exists for the opposite case: a provider that reads a family-specific key's mere presence as which record type is meant.

success.description: How to tell success from failure. Without this the executor falls back to the 2xx status code, which is wrong for DynDNS2 — it answers "badauth" with a 200.

vocabulary.description: Use a known answer vocabulary instead of a rule. "dyndns2" is the only one.

json_path_equals.description: Dotted path into a JSON answer and the value it must have, e.g. status=SUCCESS.

failures.description: Text in the answer mapped to a DNSmith error code, so the user reads a real sentence instead of the provider's raw output.

username.description: Template. {name} is replaced by a field value or by ipv4, ipv6, ip, hostname, domain, owner.

password.description: Template. {name} is replaced by a field value or by ipv4, ipv6, ip, hostname, domain, owner.

values.description: Header name to value template, for mode "headers". All of them must resolve, or the candidate does not apply.

auth.description: One way of authenticating. Several providers accept alternatives that are different requests rather than variations of one — a bearer token or the account's e-mail and password — so a list may be given instead, and the first candidate whose values are all present is used.
